text:
Bull Bear Debate Upon Earnings May 05, 2018 by Tim Link in Daily Recap
Here is a weekly recap of the S&P 500 broken down by sector (holding weightings %, YTD % and % of portfolio in top 10 holdings) followed by sector heat map after bull bear debate upon earnings. Stocks in heat map are based on the top 10 holdings of each sector ETF. Click on each picture to zoom in. Below is a summary of this week’s action on Wall Street provided by CNBC: Week in Review: Warren Buffett buys 75 million shares of Apple
Apple earnings beat, Mike Pompeo sworn in as secretary of State, and Tesla slides after Elon Musk’s “bonehead” remarks on earnings call.
The S&P 500 (SPY) lost -0.24% for the week as bull bear debate upon earnings. Sector decliners beat advancers 6 to 4 on the week as shown below in the sector graph. Healthcare (XLV) -3.04%, consumer staples (XLP) -2.13%, financials (XLF) -1.55% and industrials (XLI) -1.27% led decliners down. Consumer discretionary (XLY) and utilities (XLU) each had minor declines of less than 1%. Technology (XLK) +2.63% led advancers. Energy (XLE), materials (XLB) and real estate (XLRE) each had minor gains of less than 1%.
The Dow Jones index ended just below the flatline for the week, losing -0.18%. The Nasdaq faired a little better, gaining +1.72%.
A proposed merger having T-Mobile buying Sprint for $26.5 billion sent the telecom sector and overall market lower on Monday as investors remained skeptical on federal approval. Stocks finished mixed on Tuesday in anticipation of Apple earnings. Major indexes sold off in the last hour of trading on Wednesday as higher price inflation spooked investors after the Fed left interest rates unchanged but mentioned rising inflation. Apple (AAPL) popped more than 4% after posting great earnings. The Dow squeezed out a minor gain after rallying and coming back from a 400 point loss earlier in the session on Thursday as Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin led a group of the Trump administration to China to discuss trade issues with Chinese government officials. Legendary investor Warren Buffett sparked a massive bull rally on Friday after he disclosed he bought 75 million shares of Apple (AAPL) in addition to his current position. Friday’s rally continued despite a lackluster jobs report. The economy added 164,000 jobs in April compared to an estimate of 195,000 jobs. The unemployment rate fell below 4% to 3.9%.
Weekly performance of S&P 500 top 10 holdings… AAPL +13.25%
